column6: old text note, not changed: Explainer attributes the "unfree world" line to Camus; the attribution is common but its source is uncertain, and it is not an aphorism from a fragment collection

cut bullet 3: its correction ("much autoethnographic writing also draws on wider research") does not refute the belief, and evocative autoethnography can rest mainly on personal narrative plus analysis; 2 bullets remain

wrong answer key: item labeled "False:" with answer false, but its own explanation said "This statement is actually true"; set answer true, relabeled prompt "True or false:", fixed first explanation sentence

old text note, not changed: q:2 marks "a biographer who omits unflattering information is ... hiding truth" as true; this is overstated (its own explanation says selection is necessary) and conflicts in tone with new mis bullet 2

He doesn't invent dialogue that wasn't said is false: critics documented altered or invented scenes, most famously the closing cemetery scene; rewrote to say Capote presented the book as factual and its accuracy is debated

question said the book "proved" power "without fabricating facts" (answer true) and explanation said "The book doesn't invent"; reworded question to "built on factual research" and explanation to note the invented ending
without falsifying the record changed to "while staying grounded in reporting" for the same reason

bullet 1 correction stated as plain fact that writers "do not make up sensory experiences or events"; some practitioners do and the line is debated; reworded to "the genre's standard is that they do not"
old text note, not changed: Explainer says "Didion has written about"; she died in 2021, past tense would be better
giant water bug passage confirmed in chapter 1 of Pilgrim at Tinker Creek
bullet 2 line between documentary and fiction is somewhat simplified (staging and reenactment debates) but acceptable
landscapes in bullet 2 is the literal topic term, not the banned figurative use
The Fire Next Time does open with the letter to Baldwin's nephew ("My Dungeon Shook")
Montaigne's preface "To the Reader" does name himself as the matter of his book
Brevity is a real journal of brief nonfiction
misattribution: Robert Olen Butler and Diane Williams are known for flash fiction, not flash nonfiction; kept Dinty W. Moore and noted he founded Brevity
